_comment: Installations that are NOT live, and why. Read by `.github/scripts/lock-pinned-digests.py`
(AXIS 3) — MeshWeaver#3438 / #3858.
🚨 THIS FILE IS NOT THE ROSTER. The deployment overlays are: every `Hosting__Deployment:` a
`values*.yaml` in the fleet declares is an installation the protection run EXPECTS to answer
`/api/version`. An installation that is missing from THIS file is therefore LIVE, and a live
installation that does not answer makes the run INCOMPLETE and refuses the unlock arm. So
forgetting an entry here is always the stricter mistake, never the looser one — which is the
only direction a hand-maintained file is allowed to fail in.
What it exists for is the distinction #3858 asks for in as many words: *retirement is
explicit and auditable; a temporarily unavailable portal is not treated as retired*. A portal
that is down and a portal that was decommissioned are the same silence, and only one of them
may have its images collected. Silence is unavailability. A line here is retirement.
`state` is one of: live | not-installed | retired. Anything else is a RED, as is a non-live
entry with no `reason`, as is an entry naming an installation no overlay declares (a stale
exemption hides the next one).
🚨 `registry` IS A SCOPE STATEMENT, NOT AN EXEMPTION FROM ANSWERING. An entry carrying one is
still LIVE, still expected to answer `/api/version`, still counted — and it prints on its own
line in the report (`…declared OUT OF THIS REGISTRY'S SCOPE`) so it can never be read as
protected. The single thing it says is that this installation's images are served by a
registry `acr purge` cannot reach and this lane cannot lock, so there is nothing HERE to
protect for it. It is checked BOTH ways against what the overlay actually pins: a declaration
naming a registry the overlay does not pin in is RED, and so is one on an installation that
ALSO pins in this ACR (half in is not out). It is refused on a non-live entry, and refused
without a `reason`.
Removing an entry is how an installation re-enters the expected set.
An installation that is LIVE but not reachable from a GitHub-hosted runner is deliberately
NOT a state here. It would be an exemption meaning `this one never has to answer`, which is
the shape that goes stale silently — and the two installations measured on 2026-09-12 both
answer over the public internet. If one ever cannot, that is a decision to take then, in a
reviewed diff, and it needs its own state rather than being filed under `retired`.

instances.reason: The fleet's build server (build.meshweaver.cloud, MeshWeaver.Plugins#1784). It is LIVE and it ANSWERS — the 2026-09-13 01:18Z run read core c84c6c0 from it — but deployments/aks/build/values.build.public.yaml pins `cr.meshweaver.cloud/memex-portal-ai:3.0.0-ci.8411` and its migration twin in the FLEET'S OWN registry, which `acr purge` cannot reach and this lane cannot lock. Before this entry the ACR-scoped extractor read that overlay as pinning ZERO and the run refused with `pins no image at all` — a false sentence that reddened the lane from 2026-09-13 and, because `pause.reEnableWhen` is `lock-pinned-digests is green`, stood between the fleet and re-enabling cleanup. 🚨 WHAT RETAINS cr.meshweaver.cloud IS NOT ESTABLISHED HERE and is tracked on MeshWeaver#3438: this entry states that the images are out of THIS lane's reach, never that something else is protecting them. Delete it the day the overlay pins in this ACR again.

Declared by deployments/aks/pearl/values.pearl.public.yaml and never installed — pearl.meshweaver.cloud has no DNS record (measured 2026-09-12). Memex#219 records the same state: 'live on pearl, which has never been installed and would have seeded from an unpullable tag'. Its overlay pins are still protected on AXIS 2; what is not expected is an answer from a portal that was never stood up. Delete this entry the day it is provisioned.
